title: Why Drain Traps Lose Their Water Seal
description: When sewer odors enter a building, the primary cause is often a compromised trap seal. A P-trap holds a standing column of water that acts as a continuous physical barrier against hazardous sewer gases. However, this water seal can fail due to self-siphonage, momentum siphonage, evaporation in rarely used fixtures, or inadequate venting. Without proper Drain-Waste-Vent piping to equalize air pressure, flowing water creates negative pressure downstream, pulling liquid out of the trap. Plumbers must diagnose whether the seal loss stems from air pressure imbalances, mechanical blockages, or extended periods of inactivity.

Why Drain Traps Lose Their Water Seal

When sewer odors enter a building, the primary cause is often a compromised trap seal. A P-trap holds a standing column of water that acts as a continuous physical barrier against hazardous sewer gases. However, this water seal can fail due to self-siphonage, momentum siphonage, evaporation in rarely used fixtures, or inadequate venting. Without proper Drain-Waste-Vent piping to equalize air pressure, flowing water creates negative pressure downstream, pulling liquid out of the trap. Plumbers must diagnose whether the seal loss stems from air pressure imbalances, mechanical blockages, or extended periods of inactivity.
